aspects.fertilizer:
Application Guidelines:
Drill all phosphorus, potash, and the first nitrogen split at sowing, separate from seed.
Never drill urea.
Split nitrogen into two to three doses, or four or more doses in sandy soils.
Apply missed phosphorus or potash with the first irrigation.
Late-sown wheat receives full fertilizer at sowing.
Progressive growers apply two bags DAP per acre.
Potash boosts disease resistance, while excess nitrogen increases rust risk.
Apply gypsum before monsoon in saline soils based on chemical analysis.
Use Punjab Kissan Card and the free SFRI Lahore Khaad Hisab app.

Irrigated Soils:
Poor soil with organic matter under 0.86 percent, phosphorus under 7 ppm, and potash under 80 ppm needs 64 kg N, 46 kg P, and 25 kg K per acre. Apply 2 DAP, 2 urea, and 1 SOP or MOP bags; or 5 SSP 18 percent, 2.75 urea, and 1 SOP or MOP bags; or 3 SSP 18 percent, 2 Nitrophos, 3.25 CAN, and 1 SOP or MOP bags.
Average soil with organic matter 0.86 to 1.29 percent, phosphorus 7 to 14 ppm, and potash 80 to 180 ppm needs 54 kg N, 34 kg P, and 25 kg K per acre. Apply 1.5 DAP, 1.75 urea, and 1 SOP or MOP bags; or 3.75 SSP 18 percent, 2.25 urea, and 1 SOP or MOP bags; or 2 SSP 18 percent, 1.5 Nitrophos, 3 CAN, and 1 SOP or MOP bags.
Fertile soil with organic matter over 1.29 percent, phosphorus over 14 ppm, and potash over 180 ppm needs 46 kg N, 30 kg P, and 25 kg K per acre. Apply 1.25 DAP, 1.5 urea, and 1 SOP or MOP bags; or 3.25 SSP 18 percent, 2 urea, and 1 SOP or MOP bags; or 2 SSP 18 percent, 1.25 Nitrophos, 2.5 CAN, and 1 SOP or MOP bags.

Rain-fed Punjab:
Apply all recommended fertilizer at sowing during seedbed preparation.
Rainfall under 350 mm in Rajanpur, Layyah, DG Khan, Muzaffargarh, Bhakkar, Mianwali, Khushab barani tracts, Jand, and Pindi Gheb requires 32 kg N, 23 kg P, and 12 kg K per acre, using 1 DAP, 1 urea, and 0.5 SOP or MOP bags.
Rainfall 350 to 600 mm in Chakwal, Talagang, and Pind Dadan Khan requires 40 kg N, 28 kg P, and 12 kg K per acre, using 1.25 DAP, 1.25 urea, and 0.5 SOP or MOP bags.
Rainfall over 600 mm in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum, Sohawa, Narowal, Gujrat, Kharian, and Shakargarh requires 48 kg N, 34 kg P, and 25 kg K per acre, using 1.5 DAP, 1.5 urea, and 1 SOP or MOP bags.

Organic and Micronutrients:
Apply 5 kg zinc sulphate 33 percent and 2.5 kg boric acid 17 percent per acre at sowing, unless zinc was applied to the previous crop.
Apply 8 to 10 tons or 3 to 4 trolleys of rotted farmyard manure per acre every two to three years.
Never use raw dung because it breeds termites.
Sow Jantar, Guara, or Dhaincha in June and plow under at flowering around August 15 to 20, two months before wheat.
Before Basmati rice, plow green manure under 15 to 20 days prior to transplanting.
Incorporate crop residues using a rotavator or disc harrow, or use compost.

Bag Nutrient Content:
Each 50 kg bag supplies 23 kg N in Urea 46 percent, 13 kg N in CAN 26 percent, 11 kg N and 10 kg P in Nitrophos 22:20, 9 kg P in SSP 18 percent, 23 kg P in TSP 46 percent, 9 kg N and 23 kg P in DAP 18:46, 25 kg K in SOP 50 percent, and 30 kg K in MOP 60 percent.
aspects.harvesting:
**Harvesting and Threshing:**
Wheat harvesting occurs between April 10 and May 10.
Harvest only when the crop is fully mature.
Arrange labor, thresher, tractor, trolley, tarpaulins or plastic sheets, and combine harvester before cutting and threshing.
Stop harvesting during rain and resume only after weather improves.
Tie bundles relatively small with ears facing the same direction.
Make small threshing floors in elevated fields and dig drainage trenches around them.
Regularly inspect harvesting and threshing machinery to prevent grain breakage and loss into straw.
Do not hoe or use a bar harrow after spraying weedicide, and never use weeds as fodder.

**Crop Residues and Green Manuring:**
Never burn crop residues.
When harvesting with a combine harvester, make straw using a wheat straw chopper for extra income.
Alternatively, mix residues into the soil using a rotavator or disc harrow, or compost them to return nutrients and reduce future fertilizer requirements.
In fields with a 1.5 to 2 month gap before the next crop, such as Basmati rice areas, plant green manure crops after wheat harvest.
Recommended green manure crops are Jantar, Mung, Guar, and Rawan.
Incorporate green manure crops into the soil using a rotavator at the flowering stage before planting the next crop.

**Seed Production and Storage:**
Sow certified seed from the agriculture department or produce pure seed from the field.
Rogue out weeds and off type plants from seed fields.
Cut plants infected with loose smut and bury them in the soil.
Use straw of the same wheat variety to tie bundles and establish separate threshing floors.
Clean the thresher or harvester thoroughly and do not keep the first 1 to 2 bags as seed.
Mark the variety name clearly on seed bags.
Store seed in a bright, well ventilated warehouse with moisture not exceeding 10 percent.
Mandatorily grade seed before planting the next year.

**Grain Storage and Fumigation:**
Store grain at maximum 10 percent moisture, which is confirmed when a grain cracks sharply between teeth.
Sun dry grain if moisture is higher.
Fill warehouse cracks with cement or mud.
Spray warehouse with recommended insecticide, keep closed for at least 48 hours, and aerate for 4 to 6 hours before entry.
Use new bags, or wash old bags with recommended poison solution and dry them.
Hermetic bags or cocoons allow long term storage without fumigation.
In traditional warehouses, fumigate twice yearly at storage and after monsoon rains.
Use 30 to 35 aluminum phosphide tablets per 1000 cubic feet tied in cloth.
Keep warehouses airtight for at least 7 days, dispose of tablet ash, and aerate for 4 to 6 hours before entering.
Place recommended poison tablets on rodent runways at night.
In 1 ton home bins, place 2 to 3 tablets in a cup on top of grain, seal airtight, keep closed for at least 20 days, and fumigate twice yearly.
aspects.irrigation:
**Wheat after Cotton, Maize, or Sugarcane:**
Apply the first irrigation at crown root initiation and tillering, 20 to 25 days after sowing. Delaying it reduces tillers and spikes per plant. Apply the second irrigation at booting stage, 80 to 90 days after sowing. Delaying it reduces spike size, grain count, and yield. Apply the third irrigation at milky stage, 125 to 130 days after sowing. Delaying it reduces grain size, grain weight, and yield. Apply an extra irrigation between regular irrigations if weather remains continuously hot and dry.

**Wheat after Rice:**
Apply the first irrigation 35 to 45 days after sowing due to high residual moisture in rice stubble. This delay keeps soil soft, maintains root aeration, and boosts root and tiller growth. Apply the second irrigation at booting stage, 80 to 90 days after sowing. Apply the third irrigation at milky stage, 125 to 130 days after sowing.

**Late Sown Wheat:**
Late sown wheat requires three critical irrigations. Apply the first irrigation at tillering, 25 to 30 days after sowing. Apply the second irrigation at booting stage, 70 to 80 days after sowing. Apply the third irrigation at milky stage, 110 to 115 days after sowing.

**Thal and Hot Sandy Areas:**
Wheat requires six irrigations according to local conditions. Apply the first irrigation 20 to 25 days after sowing. Apply the second irrigation at tillering, 40 to 45 days after sowing. Apply the third irrigation at booting, 70 to 75 days after sowing. Apply the fourth irrigation at flowering, 90 to 95 days after sowing. Apply the fifth irrigation at grain formation, 110 to 115 days after sowing. Apply the sixth irrigation at grain filling, 130 to 135 days after sowing.

**Punjab Irrigation Cutoff Dates:**
Complete the final irrigation by March 15 in South Punjab. Complete the final irrigation by March 25 in North and Central Punjab. Irrigation can occur later if crop requirement and weather conditions necessitate it.

**Water Management and Climate Precautions:**
Level fields to distribute water uniformly. Divide fields into small plots after sowing to avoid excess water application. Sow on ridges in clay, poorly absorbing, or low-lying soils where water stagnates. Drain excess rainwater from fields. Check weather forecasts prior to irrigation. Provide additional irrigation during persistent dry, hot, or foggy weather. Avoid unnecessary irrigation to suppress rust attack.

**Barani Areas and Protection:**
In rain-fed barani areas, plow once with a Raja or chisel plow after the first monsoon rain, then use a common plow after subsequent rains to conserve moisture. For termites, flood recommended pesticide with irrigation water during pre-sowing rauni or after crop emergence. Apply recommended broadleaf weedicides after the first irrigation.
aspects.machinery:
Land Leveling:
Level fields with a laser land leveler for uniform input distribution, emergence, and first irrigation.

Drill Sowing and Calibration:
Sow by drill or por. Seed depth is 1.5 to 2 inches, but up to 2.5 inches in sandy soil. Separate seed and fertilizer boxes; never drill urea. Apply missing phosphorus or potash at first irrigation, or full fertilizer at sowing for late wheat. Calibrate with tube bags while driving. Divide seed weight by area (width times distance). Collecting 500 grams over an 8-foot width and 30-foot run (240 square feet, or 2.08 grams per square foot) equals roughly 90 kg per acre, needing downward adjustment. Calibrate fertilizer boxes similarly.

Sailaba Areas:
Deep plow and level. For final preparation, plow twice in heavy and loam soils, but plow once and plank in light and sandy soils.

After Cotton, Maize, and Sugarcane:
For moist method, irrigate 15 to 20 days pre-harvest. Cut stalks, plow twice, rotavate once or plank heavily, and drill. For dry method in light loam and sandy soils, plow twice, rotavate or disc harrow once, drill up to 1 inch deep, make beds, and irrigate. Avoid dry method in heavy soils.

After Rice:
Stop irrigation 15 to 25 days pre-harvest. At proper moisture, rotavate once or disc harrow twice, plow, plank, and sow. Or spread combine heaps and direct-drill using a zero-tillage drill or Super Seeder. If cut higher by combine, sow with a Pak Seeder. Never burn residues.

Bed Planting:
Bed planter machines improve drainage, deepen roots against lodging, prevent yellowing, and allow mustard intercropping.

Rain-fed Areas and Moisture Conservation:
After first monsoon rain, run a moldboard or chisel plow deep. Later, plow and plank as needed, then plow twice and plank heavily. Drill sow with full fertilizer during preparation. In barani areas, plow after harvest to destroy termite nests.

Spraying and Pest Control:
Spray using flat fan or T-jet nozzles with 100 to 120 liters water per acre. If a tank covers one-eighth acre, use eight tanks per acre with one-eighth chemical dose per tank. Spray broadleaf weeds after first irrigation, grassy weeds after second, or combined chemicals at 40 to 45 crop days. Spray in sunshine after dew dries; avoid wind, fog, or rain. In sandy or saline soil, never hoe or feed treated weeds to livestock. For termites, flood recommended poison at rauni or irrigation; avoid raw cow dung.

Harvesting and Post-Harvest Machinery:
Prepare thresher, tractor, trolley, tarpaulins, sheets, and combine harvester beforehand. Stop harvesting in rain. If combine harvested, make straw with a wheat straw chopper or rotavate residues into soil. Check machines to prevent grain breakage or straw loss. Fumigate stores before storage. If a 1.5 to 2-month gap exists, sow jenter, mung, guar, or cowpeas and rotavate at flowering.
aspects.other:
Climate Change Management:
Untimely rains and abnormal temperature fluctuations damage crops and change pest and disease attack intensity.
Climate fluctuations affect the sowing time of wheat.
Farmers must monitor weather forecasts and give special care to crop maintenance and plant protection.
Drain excess rainwater out of wheat fields.
Apply irrigation according to crop needs during drought and high temperatures.
Sow wheat varieties that have resistance against rust.
Sow wheat varieties that have relatively better resistance against lodging.
Sow wheat varieties that are adaptable to climate change.

Low-Lying and Clay Soils:
Sow wheat on ridges in clayey and low-lying lands.

Ridge Cultivation:
Wheat sown on ridges or tracks allows easy application of fertilizer and easy intercropping with crops like mustard.

Grain Consumption:
Promote multi-grain flour to balance wheat use and make flour healthier.
Mix appropriate quantities of maize, barley, and millet into wheat flour.
Mixing these grains lowers wheat consumption and makes the flour more nutritious.

Punjab Extension Activities:
In Punjab province, the Director of Agriculture Extension and Deputy Director of Agriculture Extension will prepare area-specific production plans.
These regional production plans will include production technology as well as area and yield targets.
Copies of these plans will be distributed to regional extension workers to inform them of their campaign responsibilities.
aspects.overview:
General Wheat Facts:
Wheat is the most widely cultivated crop in Pakistan. It is the primary human food source and the backbone of national food security. It is cultivated during the Rabi season and used for flour, roti, and bakery products. Approved varieties and modern technology increase production.

Punjab Production Statistics:
In 2019-20, wheat was cultivated on 16,100 thousand acres (6,515 thousand hectares), producing 19,402 thousand metric tons with an average yield of 30.13 maunds per acre (2,978 kg per hectare).
In 2020-21, area was 16,670 thousand acres (6,746 thousand hectares), total production was 20,900 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 31.34 maunds per acre (3,098 kg per hectare).
In 2021-22, area was 16,210 thousand acres (6,560 thousand hectares), total production was 20,032 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 30.89 maunds per acre (3,053 kg per hectare).
In 2022-23, area was 16,014 thousand acres (6,481 thousand hectares), total production was 21,225 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 33.14 maunds per acre (3,276 kg per hectare).
In 2023-24, area reached 17,443 thousand acres (7,059 thousand hectares), total production reached a record 23,243 thousand metric tons, and average yield reached 34.75 maunds per acre (3,435 kg per hectare).

Punjab 2023-2024 Production Factors:
Area increased by about 8.9 percent due to the government Grow More Wheat campaign, timely support price announcement, and land shifting from oilseed crops and spring maize to wheat.
Average yield increased by about 4.8 percent because early maturing rice and cotton varieties allowed timely sowing in November.
Favorable temperatures in March and April during grain formation and filling increased grain number, size, and weight.

Irrigated Wheat Varieties:
Urooj-22 was released in 2022 by the Wheat Research Institute, Faisalabad.
Dilkash-20 and Subhani-21 were released in 2021 by the Wheat Research Institute, Faisalabad.
Anaj-17 was released in 2017 by the Wheat Research Institute, Faisalabad.
Ujala-16 was released in 2016 by the Wheat Research Institute, Faisalabad.
Borlaug-16 was developed by NARC, Islamabad, and released in 2016.
Faisalabad-2008 was released in 2008 by the Wheat Research Institute, Faisalabad.

Late Sowing Impacts:
Late sowing causes daily yield declines.
Seeds take longer to germinate, plants tiller less, and ears remain small.
Excessive heat during grain formation and filling significantly cuts yield.

Irrigated and Rain-fed Extension Measures:
Effective weed control increases wheat yield by 20 to 25 percent in both barani and irrigated areas.
Each Field Assistant will establish at least one chemical and mechanical weed control demonstration plot.
Deputy Directors of Agriculture Extension will lead weed removal and proper irrigation campaigns.
Trainings with research experts will occur at district and tehsil levels for staff and farmers.
Farmer meetings will occur at tehsil, markaz, and union council levels.
Extension staff will post mottos and practices on walls, pillars, and signboards.
Field Assistants and Agriculture Officers will set up 1-acre demonstration plots following departmental recommendations on seed rate, fertilizers, weed control, and irrigation.
Information will be shared via newspapers, pamphlets, posters, radio, television, and social media from sowing to harvest.
aspects.pests_diseases:
Varieties:
Urooj-22 and Nishan-21 are approved for irrigated and rain-fed areas.
Sadiq-21 and Nawab-21 suit South Punjab.
Durum-2021 is for pasta and noodles.
Akbar-19, Nawab-21, and Zincol-16 contain higher zinc levels.
Faisalabad-2008, Pakistan-13, and Barani-17 are susceptible to rust, so cultivate them on less area.
Sow certified, rust-resistant, lodging-resistant, and climate-resilient varieties.

Seed Treatment:
Treat seed against smut, Karnal bunt, wheat blast, and foot rot.
Apply Thiophanate-methyl at 2 to 2.5 grams or Imidacloprid plus Tebuconazole at 2 milliliters per kilogram of seed.
Use a revolving drum, or shake seed and chemical inside a half-filled plastic bag.

Spraying:
Calibrate the machine with water, measure the covered area, and divide the per-acre chemical dose equally per tank.
Never hoe immediately after spraying, as this cancels chemical effects, regrows weeds, and causes farmers to inhale toxic dust.

Field Management:
Drain excess rainwater from fields.
Irrigate during drought and high temperatures.
Sow on ridges in clayey and low-lying soils.
Sow in November to minimize rust.
Avoid excessive irrigation, high seed rates, and excess nitrogen fertilizer.
Apply potash fertilizer to improve resistance.

Insect Pests:
Aphids suck sap from leaves, tillers, and ears from mid-February to March, causing black mold and shriveled grains.
Plant two lines of mustard or canola every 100 feet in wheat fields to attract predatory ladybird beetles, Chrysopa, spiders, syrphid flies, and parasites.
Spray pressurized water during severe aphid attacks.
Black ants carry away seeds at sowing; apply recommended poison dust to their nests.
Termites attack roots in patches, especially in rain-fed areas.
Flood recommended poison during pre-sowing rauni or with post-emergence irrigation.
Plow rain-fed fields after harvest to destroy termite nests, and never use raw animal manure.
Cutworm larvae cut seedlings at ground level at night; apply irrigation and recommended pesticides.
Armyworms march in groups to damage leaves and ears; dig a trench around infested fields and dust with poison.
Pink borer overwinters in rice stubble, attacks wheat in rice tracts from February to March, and causes white empty heads; destroy rice stubble and uproot infested tillers.
American bollworm attacks tillers in November to December and ears in March to April in cotton zones; deep plow after cotton harvest, destroy weeds, install light traps, and use Trichogramma cards.

Rodents and Birds:
Mix 1 part Zinc Phosphide with 20 parts flour and gur or sugar into small tablets, or mix 1 part poison with 20 parts boiled wheat grains, placing them near rat burrows at night.
Use poisonous gas tablets inside burrows, sticky cards, traps, or fill burrows with soil or water.
Keep poison away from pets and wildlife.
Crows and mynas steal seeds at sowing, while sparrows attack ripe ears in flocks.
Deter birds using scarecrows, flags, tin cans, and predatory birds.
Never use chemical poisons against birds on wheat.

Diseases:
Punjab faces wind-borne fungal yellow rust in parallel lines and brown rust in scattered spots, both favored by winter rains.
Grow three to four resistant varieties instead of a single variety.
Karnal bunt turns parts of grains into black powder at ear emergence; use crop rotation and treated certified seed.
Loose smut forms black powdery ears across Punjab, especially in rain-fed areas.
Soak seed in water for 4 to 6 hours in May or June and dry thoroughly in the sun before storing.
Uproot loose smut plants inside polythene sheets.
Foot rot attacks seedlings and mature plants in February to March; burn crop residues, avoid early sowing in risky areas, or irrigate immediately after sowing in dry soil.
Powdery mildew causes white spots on upper leaf surfaces during cold, cloudy, and humid weather; grow resistant varieties and spray approved fungicides.
Leaf blight, flag smut, and nematodes also attack wheat crops.
aspects.sowing:
General Wheat:
Average wheat yield increased 4.8 percent in 2023-24 due to November sowing and favorable March-April temperatures. High December temperatures harm early-sown wheat, while high March-April temperatures reduce late-sown yield. Sow 2 lines of mustard or canola every 100 feet for aphid control. Seed germination must be 85 percent or higher. Treat seed with fungicide for loose smut and ukhera. Ukhera second attack occurs in February to March.

Irrigated Sowing:
Optimal sowing is 1 to 20 November, extending to 30 November, with 15 November being best. Recommended late varieties can be sown until 10 December. Seed rate is 40 to 45 kg per acre until 20 November, and 50 kg per acre from 21 November to 10 December. Cut rice irrigation 15 to 25 days before harvest. Cut cotton, maize, and sugarcane irrigation 15 to 20 days before harvest. In gup-chhath, soak seed 4 to 6 hours for sandy soil; do not soak in hard or kallar soil.

Barani Sowing:
Sowing runs from 15 October to 15 November, or starts the first week of October. Seed rate is 50 kg per acre. Apply all recommended fertilizer before sowing during land preparation. In June, sow Jantar or Guara and plow down 15 to 20 August.

Balochistan Irrigated:
Sow 20 October to 30 November. Approved varieties are Zardana 89, Zarghoon 79, Umeed 2014, NIFA Lalma 2013, Aas 2011, Raskoh 2005, Punjab 2011, Benazir 2013, Ujala 2016, Johar 2016, Faisalabad 2008, Khosha 2019, Aaghaz 2019, and Zarlashta-99.

Balochistan Barani:
Sow 25 October to 30 November. Approved varieties are Raskoh 2005, Aaghaz 2019, Sariab 92, Benazir 2013, Ujala 2016, Pir Sabak 2013, and Pir Sabak 2015.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Irrigated:
Sow 1 to 30 November. Approved varieties are Khyber-2023, Pir Sabak-2023, Tarnab Rahbar, Swabi-1, Gandum Tukhm Norang-23, Khaista 2017, Israr Shaheed 2017, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 2015, Ghol, Faisalabad 2008, Pir Sabak 2008, Ghaneemat, Punjab 2011, Fakhr-e-Sarhad, Janbaz 2010, Pir Sabak 2019, Gulzar 2019, Faheem 2019, Zankol 2016, A Zarak Dera, Pir Sabak 2013, and Paseena 2017.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Barani:
Sow 20 October to 30 November. Approved varieties are Khyber-2023, Tanda-23, Taskeen-22, Pir Sabak 2015, Shahkar 2013, Tatara, NIFA Lalma 2013, Zam, NIFA, Insaf 2015, A Zarak Dera, Kohat 2017, Shahid 2017, Aman 2017, Wadan 2017, Jang 2016, and Hashim 2010.

Sowing Methods and Fertilizer:
Drill seed depth is 1.5 to 2 inches, maximum 2.5 inches in sandy soil, and maximum 1 inch in dry sowing. Separate seed and fertilizer boxes in the drill. Never drill urea. Apply unapplied phosphorus or potash with the first irrigation. For late sowing, apply the full fertilizer dose at sowing.
aspects.varieties:
**Irrigated Punjab:**
Sow from November 1 to 20, up to November 30, or until December 10 for late crops. Seed rate is 40 to 45 kg per acre before November 20, and 50 kg from November 21 to December 10. Recommended varieties are Urooj-22, Nishan-21, Dilkash-20, Subhani-21, MH-21, Durum-2021, Sadiq-21, Nawab-21, NARC Super, Rahbar-21, Akbar-19, Bhakkar Star-19, Ghazi-19, Fakhar Bhakkar-17, Anaj-17, Ujala-16, Zincol-16, Borlaug-16, Johar-16, and Faisalabad-2008. Sadiq-21 and Ghazi-19 grains are amber; all other varieties have eastern reddish grains. Sadiq-21 and Nawab-21 are best suited for South Punjab. Akbar-19, Nawab-21, and Zincol-16 are rich in zinc. Durum-2021 is reserved for industrial pasta and noodle products. Faisalabad-2008 is susceptible to rust, so cultivate it on less area.

**Rain-fed Punjab:**
Sow from October 15 to November 15, or as early as the first week of October. Seed rate is 50 kg per acre. Recommended varieties are Urooj-22, Nishan-21, MA-21, Markaz-19, Barani-17, Fatehjang-16, and Pakistan-13. Pakistan-13 and Barani-17 are susceptible to rust. Urooj-22 and Nishan-21 are approved for both irrigated and rain-fed zones.

**Variety Yields:**
Yield potentials in maunds per acre are 75 to 80 for Bhakkar Star-19 and Anaj-17; 76 for Urooj-22; 75 for Nishan-21, Akbar-19, Fakhar Bhakkar-17, and Ujala-16; 72 for Pakistan-13 and Borlaug-16; 71 for Dilkash-20; 70 for Subhani-21, MH-21, Durum-2021, Sadiq-21, Nawab-21, NARC Super, and Johar-16; 65 to 70 for Ghazi-19; 60 to 75 for Rahbar-21; 65 for Zincol-16 and Markaz-19; 61 for Barani-17 and Faisalabad-2008; and 60 for MA-21 and Fatehjang-16.

**Balochistan:**
Irrigated sowing runs October 20 to November 30 with Zardana-89, Zarghoon-79, Umeed-2014, Nifa Lalma-2013, Aas-2011, Raskoh-2005, Punjab-2011, Benazir-2013, Ujala-2016, Johar-2016, Faisalabad-2008, Khosha-2019, Aaghaz-2019, and Zarlashta-99. Rain-fed sowing runs October 25 to November 30 with Raskoh-2005, Aaghaz-2019, Sariab-92, Benazir-2013, Ujala-2016, Pir Sabak-2013, and Pir Sabak-2015.

**Khyber Pakhtunkhwa:**
Irrigated sowing runs November 1 to 30 with Khyber-2023, Pir Sabak-2023, Tarnab Rahbar, Swabi-1, Gandum Tukhm Norang-23, Khaista-2017, Israr Shaheed-2017, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa-2015, Goal, Faisalabad-2008, Pir Sabak-2008, Ghanimat, Punjab-2011, Fakhr-e-Sarhad, Janbaz-2010, Pir Sabak-2019, Gulzar-2019, Fahim-2019, Zincol-2016, AZRC Dera, Pir Sabak-2013, and Paseena-2017. Rain-fed sowing runs October 20 to November 30 with Khyber-2023, Tanda-23, Taskeen-22, Pir Sabak-2015, Shahkar-2013, Tatara, Nifa Lalma-2013, Zam, NIFA, Insaf-2015, AZRC Dera, Kohat-2017, Shahid-2017, Aman-2017, Wadan-2017, Jang-2016, and Hashim-2010.

**Sindh:**
Irrigated varieties are TD-1, IV-3, IV-2, TJ-83, Akbar-19, and Benazir-2013. Rain-fed varieties are Sarsabz, Kiran-95, Marvi-2000, TD-1, and Moomal-2002.

**Crop Management:**
Treat seed with Thiophanate-methyl at 2 to 2.5 grams per kg or Imidacloprid plus Tebuconazole at 2 ml per kg. Ensure seed germination is 85 percent or higher, and storage moisture is below 10 percent. Weed control raises yields by 20 to 25 percent. Against loose smut, soak seed in water for 4 to 6 hours during May or June and dry under sun. In gup-chhat sowing following cotton, maize, or sugarcane, plow twice, plank heavily, make ridges, irrigate, and broadcast 4 to 6 hours soaked seed in sandy soil, or unsoaked seed on hard saline soil after water infiltrates.
aspects.weeds:
**Rain-fed Areas:**
In June, sow green manure crops like Jantar and Guara. 
Plow them into the soil after about two months between August 15 and August 20 to improve soil fertility, conserve moisture, and control weeds. 
Growing Kharif crops increases soil fertility, moisture retention capacity, and helps control weeds. 
After the first monsoon rain, run a moldboard soil-turning plow or chisel plow deeply to absorb maximum rainwater. 
Before sowing wheat, plow and plank as needed to eliminate weeds and retain moisture. 
Before sowing, plow twice with a common plow and apply heavy planking to bring moisture to the upper soil layer. 
Sow wheat using a drill. 
Apply the entire recommended quantity of fertilizer during land preparation before sowing.

**Non-Chemical Weed Control:**
Rotate crops and cultivate fodder like berseem in wheat fields every two to three years. 
If possible, run a double bar harrow after the first irrigation when the field reaches workable moisture condition. 
For small areas, perform dry hoeing using a khurpa or kasola after crop emergence if labor is available.

**Chemical Weed Control:**
Use recommended weedicides advised by Agriculture Extension or Pest Warning staff. 
Spray recommended herbicides for broadleaf weeds after the first irrigation. 
Spray weedicides for narrowleaf grassy weeds after the second irrigation. 
Apply combination herbicides that destroy both broadleaf and grassy weed types at crop age 40 to 45 days. 
Use herbicides cautiously in sandy and kallar saline soils.

**Spraying Instructions:**
Always calibrate the spray machine before use. 
Use a water volume of 100 to 120 liters per acre. 
Use a flat fan or T-jet nozzle. 
Spray during sunshine after dew has dried off the leaves. 
Do not spray during high winds, fog, or rain. 
Do not spray any spot twice, and do not leave any area unsprayed. 
Never use sprayed weeds as animal fodder. 
Do not perform hoeing or use a bar harrow immediately after spraying. 
Hoeing breaks the chemical effect, allows weeds to regrow, and creates flying dust containing poison that severely damages farmer breathing and health.

**Yield Impact and Extension Campaign:**
Weeds reduce wheat yields in both rain-fed and irrigated areas. 
Controlling weeds effectively increases wheat yields by 20 to 25 percent using existing resources. 
Each Field Assistant will establish at least one chemical and mechanical weed control demonstration plot in their circle. 
Deputy Directors of Agriculture Extension will lead district campaigns on weed eradication and proper irrigation. 
Deputy Directors and Assistant Directors of Agriculture Extension will organize district and tehsil level trainings with wheat research and adaptive research experts for extension staff and farmers. 
Farmer gatherings will be held at tehsil, markaz, and union council levels to introduce new wheat varieties and farming practices.
